subject: design-technology
title: Foundations of the Design Process
welcome_lead: Pick up your sketchbook and follow the iterative loop from research all the way to refinement.
meta_desc: Learn the iterative design cycle and ACCESSFM for GCSE Design & Technology.
final_note: You can map any project onto the iterative cycle and use ACCESSFM as an analysis tool.

concepts.def: Looping cycle of design, test and refine.
List of measurable criteria a product must meet.
Generating many design ideas, often by sketching.
A working model used to test a design.
Analysis tool: Aesthetics, Cost, Customer and more.
Judging how well a product meets its.

walkthroughs.body_html: The iterative cycle runs: research → → ideation → prototyping → testing → evaluation → refinement. Each loop produces a better version. Unlike a linear process, designers happily revisit earlier stages when test results reveal a flaw.
ACCESSFM stands for Aesthetics, Cost, Customer, Environment, Size, Safety, Function and Materials. Apply it to a kettle: cost £25, customer is a household, function must boil 1L of water quickly.
A for a child's lunchbox might say: capacity 1L (size), under £8 (cost), made from food-safe polymer (materials), bright colours (aesthetics), watertight seal (function). Each line is testable.
